chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Umm Sa'id al-Ahmasiyyah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said: 'It is equal to one Hajj and one 'Umrah, and this much is from the good.' And he gestured with his hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), establishing the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as a locus of immense spiritual merit where physical visitation yields the combined reward of Hajj and 'Umrah. The Imam’s gesture underscores the tangible, cumulative nature of this reward, reflecting the Shia theological emphasis on the intercessory and sanctifying power of the Ahl al-Bayt's resting places. This hadith serves as a foundational text for the devotional practice of Ziyarah, linking earthly pilgrimage to eternal spiritual gain.
